llm.summary: This is a documentation-based procurement assistant with sensitive but disclosed bid-workflow behavior and no executable code or hidden exfiltration.

dimensions.detail: The skill is coherently focused on procurement notice analysis, bid planning, draft generation, and compliance review; it explicitly keeps final bid decisions, pricing, commitments, signing, and submission under human control.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The README uses broad natural-language trigger examples, but they remain procurement-specific; the artifacts also require repeated legal/author notices, which is intrusive but disclosed rather than hidden.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is documented as a manual copy into a skills folder; the package contains Markdown/YAML/JSON text files and no executable scripts or package-install hooks.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill expects procurement files, company qualifications, historical bids, pricing, and business strategy materials, which are sensitive but proportionate to the stated bidding workflow; one template asks for key-person and relationship context, so users should keep that within legal and ethical procurement boundaries.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Artifacts mention logging, archiving, reminders, and knowledge-base updates as workflow concepts, but there is no implemented background worker, persistence mechanism, autostart behavior, or privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only where procurement and company bid materials are allowed to be processed by the agent. Use explicit invocation for this skill, avoid uploading confidential bid files unless authorized, redact unnecessary personal contact details in examples or outputs, and require human review for pricing, commitments, signatures, complaints, and final submissions.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger examples are real, but they are scoped to procurement tasks and do not by themselves grant hidden access or autonomous authority.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The example case includes named public-sector contacts, phone numbers, and email addresses; this is a privacy and reuse concern, but it is static example content and not evidence of exfiltration or malicious behavior.
[unicode-control-chars] expected: The only control-format character found was a zero-width joiner in an emoji/author line, not obfuscated instructions.
